name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 partisan lean makes the seat overwhelmingly Democratic
Ford's large fundraising edge; Koppie reports just $42 on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
Open seat with no public polling adds uncertainty to the margin size
model.rationale: The district's 34-point Democratic lean, La Shawn Ford's dominant fundraising position against a Republican with almost no cash, and market pricing near 98% make a Democratic hold overwhelming despite the open seat and roughly $2.5 million in outside spending against Ford.
model.watch: A wave of additional outside spending against Ford or sharply uneven Democratic turnout could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 7th District, anchored in Chicago, is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 34 points toward Democrats. Danny Davis's retirement leaves the seat open, but the Democratic nominee, La Shawn Ford, enters the general election with a large financial advantage: he has raised about $816,000, while Republican Chad Koppie has raised under $60,000 and reports just $42 on hand. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, and outside groups have spent about $2.5 million opposing Ford, which adds some uncertainty to the size of the margin. Still, the district's fundamentals, the candidates' resource gap, and market pricing all point to the seat staying in Democratic hands by a wide margin in November.
